name: Black Combe
documented: "Half the view is the glittering sea, with the Isle of Man seen clearly to the west"

name: Dunkery Beacon
documented: "views over the surrounding moorland, the Bristol Channel and hills"

name: Pendle Hill
documented: George Fox, 1652: "I saw the sea bordering upon Lancashire"; "On a clear day, spectacular 360 degree views stretch to the sea"

name: Leith Hill (tower top)
documented: "on a clear day you can see the English Channel to the south"
source: National Trust, Visiting Leith Hill Tower (retrieved 2026)

name: Ditchling Beacon
documented: "360-degree views across the weald and out to the English Channel"
source: South Downs National Park Authority, Bird's Eye View (retrieved 2026)

name: Brown Willy
documented: "Views from the summit stretch to both sides of the coast, from Looe in the south, to Tintagel in the north"

name: Worcestershire Beacon
documented: "Parts of a dozen or so counties can be seen, and the Bristol Channel"

name: Snowdon (Yr Wyddfa)
documented: "On exceptionally clear days, Ireland, Scotland, England, and the Isle of Man are all visible" (across the Irish Sea)

name: Scafell Pike
documented: "On a clear day you can see tops in Northern Ireland, Scotland, Wales, and the Isle of Man" (across the Irish Sea)
source: UKHillwalking, One Minute Mountain: Scafell Pike (retrieved 2026)

name: Slieve Donard
documented: "In very clear conditions the Galloway Hills, Isle of Man and the Wicklow Mts are visible" (across the Irish Sea)
